name: Antipodal Link Descent Fails
statement: The twelve-state, five-dimensional family $\mathcal H_\star=\mathcal J_{5,3}^0$ is a contraction-minimal nonlearning partial cube with a unique antipodal pair and is a semicube of a learning-space graph. Nevertheless, none of its ten one-coordinate links is both antipodal and nonlearning. Hence a nonlearning antipodal family need not have a smaller link with both properties.
proof: Direct rooted-union witnesses invalidate both complementary endpoint roots, while the critical-antipodal pendant theorem gives contraction minimality and embeds the family as a positive semicube of a learning space. Exhausting the two links in each coordinate shows that every link containing an antipodal pair has a valid root; the source records their dimensions, orders, antipodal-pair counts, and valid-root counts.
